processing_steps.atmosphere: vacuum induction melted under argon (ingot cast)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by vacuum induction furnace; then homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h.
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm; plates then cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples by electrical discharge machining.
Parent solution-treatment step (state proc_st-1100c-10min-oq) prior to aging.
This is the defining aging condition of the current sample (17Al aged at 525 °C for 1 h), followed by water quenching.

structures.overall_structure: α (BCC) matrix retained after solution treatment with only a very small amount of β-Mn precipitated after aging at 525 °C for 1 h; the α→β-Mn transformation is far from complete at this low temperature and short time for the 17Al alloy

microstructure_list.region: α matrix with β-Mn precipitate at α grain boundaries

phases_present.morphology: sparse precipitate along α grain boundaries

measurement_conditions.test_standard: Vickers microhardness, load 9.8 N for 15 s, each sample tested 5 times, hardness value given by average of 5 measurements

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester, load 9.8 N for 15 s
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: each sample repeatedly tested 5 times; hardness values given by the average of 5 measurements; specimen 10 × 5 × 2 mm³
characterization_methods.purpose: measure the Vickers hardness of the 17Al alloy after aging at 525 °C for 1 h
characterization_methods.key_findings: 17Al aged at 525 °C for 1 h has a Vickers hardness of 566.9 ± 9.7 HV (much lower than the 259.8 ± 1.5 HV solution-treated baseline only slightly exceeded; the peak of 924.9 HV for 17Al is reached at 575 °C / 6 h)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: electrolytically polished using a mixture of 10 % perchloric acid and 90 % ethanol; main field scale bars 50 µm, insets 2 µm or 10 µm
characterization_methods.purpose: observe precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn and β-Mn) in aged 17Al samples including the 525 °C / 1 h condition
characterization_methods.key_findings: For 17Al aged at 525 °C for 1 h, only a sparse β-Mn precipitate was observed at an α grain boundary (Fig. 8, panel 525 °C - 1 h); precipitation is very slow at 525 °C for the 17Al alloy

unmapped_findings: For the 17Al alloy, at the low aging temperature of 525 °C the hardness increases only gradually and the alloy fails to reach its peak hardness (b0038); the 525 °C series remains the lowest of all aging temperatures (~570-620 HV at 10 h) (figure_002).

The increase in Al content significantly slows the aging hardening response: at aging temperatures from 525 °C to 575 °C the aging hardening response of the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu alloys significantly slowed down with increasing Al content (b0038).

For the 17Al and 19Al alloys aged at 525 °C, the precipitation of β-Mn was very slow compared to the 15Al alloy, and only a small amount of β-Mn was observed even after 10 h of aging (b0053); this behavior is consistent with the 17Al 525 °C / 10 h EBSD result where only 20.5 % β-Mn formed along α grain boundaries and within α grains, with some small α-Mn particles in the α matrix (b0041).
